_: 生成的動態版。人工檔，機器不覆寫。⚠️ 這是這個 repo 唯一一層**生成出來的東西**，規矩比別層更嚴。
_rule: 🔴 這一層有兩種東西，**差別在宣稱，不在畫面好不好看**：
① kind=atmosphere　宣稱「**那幅畫**動起來了」⇒ 只動氛圍不動內容，逐幀量過構圖沒被動到（位移 <16）才收。
② kind=reinterpretation　宣稱「模型**照那幅畫重畫**了一段」⇒ 可以重畫，但 differs 要逐條寫出它改了什麼，而且那份清單會印在玩家的面板上。
⛔ 唯一不准的事：把 ② 說成 ①。重畫本身不是罪，冒充原作才是。
⛔ 也不准把重畫得最明顯的那幾秒剪掉，只留看起來像原畫的片段——那是把 ② 化妝成 ①（這件事考慮過，記在 _decision）。
🔴 畫面上固定標「AI 重繪・非原作」，⛔ 不做成預設視圖。
🔴 不進畫卷、不進收藏、不算進度。收進畫帖的永遠是真跡與像素版。⇒ 也**不是收藏的獎勵**：沒收過那幅也看得到（把重繪當成收到真跡的獎賞，等於說重繪才是寶）。
🔑 這一層的『出處』＝**可重現**：模型、日期、prompt、來源圖、切回原框的座標、量到的位移，全部記在下面。指不出這些就不該放進來。
_why_this_one: no.50 御厩橋雷雨：閃電與雨本來就是那幅畫的主角，動起來不會多出任何東西；而且它是清親最有名的光線之一。⛔ 反過來說，60 兩国大火 不選——那幅的標註全是人（逃跑的人、挑擔的人、人影），模型很容易讓他們動起來。

clips.prompt:
Bring this Japanese woodblock print to life as a vivid animated scene. It is a print of Meiji-era Tokyo by Kobayashi Kiyochika (1876-1881), placed on a plain beige background.

CAMERA: The camera stays locked on the print for the whole clip, so the print's outer edges never move. Everything inside the picture is free to move.

ACTION: The rickshaw puller sprints toward the viewer, legs pumping, and the red-wheeled rickshaw rolls forward with its wheels spinning. The woman riding in it grips her parasol as her sleeves and the parasol flutter in the rush of air. Cherry blossom petals shake loose from the trees and drift across the brick avenue. In the background, the horse-drawn carriage trots away down the street, and pedestrians stroll under the colonnade of the Western-style buildings.

LIFE: Motion is clearly visible from the very first second and keeps going for the whole clip. People and animals move with readable, natural actions; clothing, hair, banners, branches, water and weather react to movement and wind. Figures may walk further, turn and interact, and other passers-by may move through the scene.

STYLE: It still looks like a moving woodblock print: flat printed colour, carved outlines, paper texture and Kiyochika's palette. Everything belongs to 1870s-1880s Tokyo: period clothing, vehicles and buildings. No photorealism and no 3D rendering.

_decision.q: 兩支 Veo 片子都被判定「重畫」而不收。但效果很好，看不太出差異——重畫真的是不能收的理由嗎？
a: 🔑 **不是。** 「重畫」是一個量測結果，「不收」是一個決定，前面兩次把這兩件事混成一句話了。
量到的是真的：位移尖峰 17–19，眼睛也對得上（黃色團塊閃電被換成分叉白閃、多出一個撐傘的人、雨線變密、天空偏藍）。
但那只證明「它不是那幅畫動起來」，不證明「它不能放進這個遊戲」。前者靠量測，後者靠**怎麼掛牌**。
⇒ 改成掛成 ②：明講它是模型重畫的另一件作品，差在哪一條一條寫出來給玩家看。
⛔ 途中想過一條歪路：整支 9.9s 裡有 2.1s 位移只有 6–10（看起來像沒重畫），本來要剪那一段來用。
去看那幾格才發現——6.5s 那一格的閃電**就是那道分叉白閃**，7.4s 與 8.3s 則是閃電整個不見。
位移量不出來，是因為閃電只佔畫面一小塊，邊的位置平均下來沒跳。⇒ 剪片只會做出一支「看起來比較沒重畫」的片子，
位移量不出來，是因為閃電只佔畫面一小塊，邊的位置平均下來沒跳。⇒ 剪片只會做出一支「看起來比較沒重畫」的片子，那正是把 ② 化妝成 ①。**指標低不等於忠實**——同一型的錯這個 repo 犯過好幾次（見 README〈五個「看起來合理」的錯〉），共同點都是：指標看起來過關，就不再去看它到底在量什麼。

_prompt_template._: 通用提示詞：一段固定的 base ＋ 依這一景的資料挑出的 motion 句子。⛔ 每次生成都逐字用這裡的版本，逐字記進 clips[].prompt（那是出處）。改了模板要在這裡留紀錄，不要即興改。　寫法與理由的筆記：docs/ai-motion-prompts.md
_prompt_template.base:
Animate this exact image. It is a Japanese woodblock print from the Meiji era (Kobayashi Kiyochika, 1876-1881), placed on a plain beige background.

CAMERA: Locked-off static shot for the whole clip. No pan, tilt, zoom, push-in, parallax, rotation or reframing. The entire print stays in frame, including its paper margins, printed title and red seal. The plain background around the print stays plain and empty.

KEEP IDENTICAL: Every person, boat, vehicle, animal, building, bridge, tree, pole and sign keeps its exact position, pose, shape and number from the first frame to the last. Nothing enters, leaves or appears. The carved outlines, flat areas of printed colour, colour palette and paper texture stay exactly as printed.

WHAT MOVES: {MOTION}

STYLE: The motion stays inside the woodblock look: flat printed colour, no photographic lighting, no 3D depth, no motion blur, no added grain, no colour grading. Movement is slow, subtle and continuous. The clip loops seamlessly: the last frame matches the first frame.

motion.rain: The rain already drawn in the print keeps falling at the same angle and the same density; it does not get heavier. Wet ground and water catch a faint flicker of reflected light.
motion.snow: The snow already drawn in the print keeps drifting down slowly at the same density. Snow lying on roofs and on the ground does not change.
motion.night: The scene stays as dark as printed.
motion.lamp: Lamps, lanterns and lit windows that are already in the print flicker very gently, in brightness only.
motion.dusk: The existing evening sky glows and fades very slightly; its colours stay as printed.
motion.dawn: The existing morning sky brightens very slightly; its colours stay as printed.
motion.moon: Moonlight on the existing water shimmers gently; the moon itself stays fixed.
motion.fireworks: The fireworks already in the sky pulse gently in brightness; their shapes stay as printed.
motion.fire: The flames and smoke already drawn in the print flicker and billow slowly in place; they do not spread or grow.
motion.bolt: The lightning keeps exactly its printed shape, size, position and colour; only its brightness pulses, and the whole scene brightens briefly in sync once or twice.
motion.default: Almost nothing moves. Existing clouds drift a tiny amount and existing water shimmers faintly. If the print has no sky or water, the whole image stays still apart from a barely perceptible breathing of light.

pick: 🔴 motion 句子**從資料挑，不看圖猜**（跟 src/weather.js 同一套證據）：
conditions.weather ∈ rain／snow／fire／moon／fireworks → 同名句子；conditions.time_of_day ∈ night／dusk／dawn → 同名句子（day 不加）。
details 的標註名含 燈・灯・火・光・明 → lamp；含 閃電・稲妻・雷 → bolt。
符合的全部接起來，順序照上面 motion 的鍵；一個都沒有 → 只用 default。
例：no.50 御厩橋雷雨＝rain＋lamp＋bolt。63 景的分佈：35 景至少有一句、28 景只有 default（唯一一景 day 不加句子，算在後者）。

settings.input: 原畫墊成 16:9 的圖當第一幀（墊邊色 #C6B993 米色，數字記在 _pad）。⚠️ 背景那句就是在防模型把畫面往墊邊外面畫出去。
settings.duration: 8 秒（Flow 的 Veo 預設；make-motion.py 會做無縫循環）
settings.language: 英文。模型對英文指令的遵從最穩；中文說明留在這個檔案裡給人看。

why: 每一句都對著前兩次 Veo 的失敗寫：
Nothing enters, leaves or appears ← 倉庫旁多出撐傘的人
lightning keeps exactly its printed shape…colour ← 黃色團塊被換成分叉白閃
does not get heavier ← 雨線變密
colour palette…stay exactly as printed ← 天空被打亮成偏藍
carved outlines…stay exactly ← 輪廓被重描、刀痕變淡
plain background stays plain ← 墊邊被當成畫面延伸
⛔ **不點名不想要的東西**（不寫 no umbrella、no branching lightning、no extra people）：影片模型對被提到的名詞很敏感，點名常常反而把它畫出來。一律用「維持原樣／不出現新東西」這種不帶名詞的說法。
⛔ 不寫 no watermark：浮水印是平台加的，提示詞擋不掉，寫了只是多一個名詞。
🔑 **提示詞只能減少重畫，擋不住重畫**（見 _attempts 的 lesson）。所以生成之後照舊跑 make-motion.py 量位移、看幀、寫 differs——模板不是替代那一關的東西。
⚠️ fire 那 4 景風險最高：標註全是人（逃的人、挑擔的人），模型最容易讓人動起來。default 那 28 景則是動得最少、最可能不值得做。先做那 35 景裡非 fire 的 31 景。

street._: 變體 B：街景版——讓畫裡的人動起來。🔴 用這個變體生出來的一律 kind=reinterpretation，differs 至少要寫「人物在走動」。
street.use_when: 畫面主體是街上的人與車（例：no.72 大傳馬町大丸），而且作者要的是熱鬧、不是忠實。⛔ 不用在火災那 4 幅：那是逃難的人，動起來就是替清親演一場災難。
street.base:
Animate this exact image. It is a Japanese woodblock print from the Meiji era (Kobayashi Kiyochika, 1876-1881), placed on a plain beige background.

CAMERA: Locked-off static shot for the whole clip. No pan, tilt, zoom, push-in, parallax, rotation or reframing. The entire print stays in frame, including its paper margins, printed title and red seal. The plain background around the print stays plain and empty.

KEEP IDENTICAL: Every building, roof, shop curtain, sign, lettering, pole, wire, lamp post and the street itself keeps its exact position, shape and colour. The printed title, signature and seal stay exactly as printed. The carved outlines, flat areas of printed colour, colour palette and paper texture stay exactly as printed.

WHAT MOVES: {MOTION}

STYLE: The motion stays inside the woodblock look: flat printed colour, no photographic lighting, no 3D depth, no motion blur, no added grain, no colour grading. Movement is slow, subtle and continuous. The clip loops seamlessly: the last frame matches the first frame.
street.motion: The people and vehicles already in the print come gently to life. They walk, pull and carry at an unhurried pace, in the directions their poses already suggest. Each figure keeps its clothing, colours and flat printed look. The street stays exactly as busy as printed, with the same number of people throughout.
street.pick: {MOTION} ＝ 上面這句 motion ＋ 主表裡依資料挑出的句子（rain／snow／night／lamp…）。⛔ 不接 default（它說 Almost nothing moves，跟這個變體互相矛盾）。
why: 跟主模板差在兩處：KEEP IDENTICAL 把「人、車不准動」換成「建築、招牌、文字、題字落款不准動」；WHAT MOVES 放人。
CAMERA 一字不改——p.72.mp4 被裁掉題字與紙邊，就是因為沒墊 16:9；人可以動，框不能動。
the same number of people throughout ← p.72.mp4 裡人越走越多（紅衣小孩、撐傘的人、左邊兩個女子）
in the directions their poses already suggest ← 讓動作從原畫的姿勢延伸，不是模型另外編排
Each figure keeps its clothing, colours and flat printed look ← 人一動，模型最容易把人畫成動畫風或照片感

overrides._: 資料（題名判出的天候與時刻）沒寫、但畫面上明明白白看得到的，才加在這裡，**一定寫理由**。只影響提示詞，⛔ 不改 views.json 的 conditions（遊戲的收景閘門照舊只看題名）。看不準的不加。

9.why: 題名「梅若神社」沒寫雨，但整幅是斜落的雨線、撐傘披簑的人與地上的水花——畫的就是雨天。

vivid._: 變體 C：生動版。每一幅寫具體的動作指令，讓畫面真的動起來。🔴 用這個變體生出來的一律 kind=reinterpretation。
why: 2026-09-15 Aaron 回報：用主模板與街景版生成，模型「幾乎沒有產生太大動畫效果，失去 AI 動畫的實質意義」。
原因在提示詞本身：Almost nothing moves／KEEP IDENTICAL／Nothing enters, leaves or appears／slow, subtle／last frame matches first frame——每一句都在壓動作。
而這一層上架的一律是「AI 重繪・非原作」＋逐條差異清單（見 _rule 與 _decision），忠實本來就不是它的承諾 ⇒ 不必再用提示詞綁住它。
保留的只有兩樣：①鏡頭鎖在原畫的外框上——make-motion.py 要照 _pad 切回原畫的框，遊戲面板也照原畫的比例放影片；②木版的畫風與明治的時代感。
拿掉循環要求：它會讓模型把動作收回原位。代價是頭尾差更多，循環接點的重疊會更明顯（見 no.72 的 known_flaw）。
動作寫法：主詞＋動詞＋方向（the puller runs toward the viewer），不寫形容詞堆疊；每一幅 4–6 個動作，前景一個主角、背景一兩樣、天候或光一樣。
⚠️ 場景句是**作者寫的演出指示**，不是對原畫的陳述，所以可以看圖寫（主模板的「從資料挑、不看圖猜」是為了忠實版）。天候仍以資料為準，資料沒寫但畫面明白看得到的走 overrides。

no.41–49 的演出句（2026-09-20，第五版模板）：41 螢火、42 煙火的火星與紅燈籠、43 水紋與蘆葦、44 雲與船、46 樹與河面、47 電線與行人、49 雨後的水紋與蘆葦——動感一律放在大面積或數量多的東西上，人物只做小動作（第五版模板已經鎖住鏡頭、色塊與人物大小）。47 的人力車朝行人走 ⇒ 照 21／27 的寫法改成「拉幾步、放慢、停下」。⛔ no.45、48 沒座標略過；no.50 御厩橋雷雨已經有忠實版的片子，不再做生動版。

vivid.base:
Animate this exact image as a vivid, lively scene. It is a Japanese woodblock print of Meiji-era Tokyo by Kobayashi Kiyochika (1876-1881), placed on a plain beige background.

CAMERA: Locked-off static shot for the whole clip: no zoom, push-in, pan or reframing. The whole print, with its paper margins, stays fully in view at the same size from the first frame to the last. Everything inside the picture is free to move.

CONTINUITY: This is one continuous shot of this one place, with no cut, dissolve or transition to another scene. The picture keeps the same layout from the first frame to the last. Within that same place, everything is free to move as described below.

KEEP: The carved outlines, the flat areas of printed colour, the palette and the paper texture stay exactly as printed. The people, animals and things already in the picture keep their size and their places in the frame. The overall colour tint of the print and the tone of its paper stay exactly as in the first frame.

ACTION: {SCENE}

LIFE: Motion is clearly visible from the very first second and keeps going for the whole clip. The people and animals already in the picture move with readable, natural actions and stay in view; clothing, hair, branches, water and weather react to movement and wind. The number of people stays the same from start to finish.

STYLE: It still looks like a moving woodblock print: flat printed colour, carved outlines, paper texture and Kiyochika's palette. Everything belongs to 1870s-1880s Tokyo: period clothing, vehicles and buildings. No photorealism and no 3D rendering.

scenes.1: The rickshaw puller sprints toward the viewer, legs pumping, and the red-wheeled rickshaw rolls forward with its wheels spinning. The woman riding in it grips her parasol as her sleeves and the parasol flutter in the rush of air. Cherry blossom petals shake loose from the trees and drift across the brick avenue. In the background, the horse-drawn carriage trots away down the street, and pedestrians stroll under the colonnade of the Western-style buildings.
scenes.2: The chestnut horse gallops at full speed in front of the bridge in a flying gallop for the entire clip, as Kiyochika drew it mid-stride: its front and hind legs reach far out and snap back together in a fast, powerful rhythm, its body stretched long and low, mane and tail streaming straight back. The rider leans forward low over the horse's neck, the red plume on the hat whipping in the wind. The runner on the right sprints flat out, arms pumping, both feet leaving the ground with each stride. Spray flies up from the wet ground under the hooves, the moat water ripples, and the pines on the bank sway in the wind.
scenes.3: The ferryman leans on his long pole and pushes, and the ferry glides across the wide river from left to right, leaving a widening wake. The three passengers sway with the boat and turn their heads to talk. A white gull skims low over the water on the right, dips and rises again, and a bird circles high above. The far shore keeps its dark groves and the small red-walled house; as the evening deepens, a warm lamp light begins to glow in that house and the sky above the trees slowly darkens.
scenes.4: Heavy snow falls and swirls across the whole scene. The traveller under the large straw umbrella trudges toward the viewer through deep snow, leaning into the wind, snow sliding off the umbrella. Behind, small figures and rickshaws make their way past the snow-covered bank building. Crows flap across the grey sky, and clumps of snow drop from the bare willow branches beside the stone bridge.
scenes.5: The sunset sky shifts from pink to deep orange and violet as the long bands of cloud drift slowly across it. The woman carrying a bundle on her back walks steadily along the path beside the canal. The tall grasses and reeds sway in the evening breeze, and the canal water ripples, stretching and breaking the reflection of the house. A lamp is lit inside the house and its windows begin to glow.
scenes.6: The painting on its easel stays standing in the middle of the path, and the people gathered around it lean in to look at it and talk about it: the woman in the yellow coat bends toward the picture, and the small child in yellow points at it and hops on the spot. Further along the path, a few people stroll slowly toward the great torii. Cherry and yellow blossoms drift down from the trees and the branches sway gently. The soft spring haze stays over the whole park, drifting slowly.
scenes.7: Thick snow falls through the dark sky. In the foreground, closest to us, the person under the very large white umbrella walks slowly away up the street, the umbrella tilting in the wind. On the left, the man in the purple coat with the white bundle on his back and the small figure under the grey umbrella trudge on through the snow. On the right, a man leans hard into the red-wheeled cart piled with its round pink load and pushes it forward, and the person under the orange umbrella walks beside it. Distant figures hurry along the wide street, and the telegraph wires sway in the wind.
scenes.8: The crows perched on the bare branches suddenly take off and fly across the twilight sky. The tall bare tree and the grasses sway in a cold evening wind. Mist drifts slowly across the flat rice fields behind the torii. The glowing disc low in the sky grows brighter as the light fades, and the shadows of the huts deepen.
scenes.9: Strong gusts drive the slanting rain across the whole picture, and the whole print keeps its dense slanting rain lines and rough hatched texture. On the left, the thatched teahouse with its white signboards stands in the downpour, and the rickshaw parked in front of it, with its blue-grey rain cover and red wheels, rocks slightly in the wind. In the middle, the small figure in the red kimono hurries toward the wooden shrine gate with the tall name post, the straw rain cape blown up and flapping behind them. The big pine above the gate and the trees on the right thrash in the wind, the tall standing stone stays upright among the bushes, and two dark birds are tossed about in the sky. Rain splashes up from the puddles on the muddy ground.
scenes.10: Red and purple maple leaves fall and drift through the air under the tall cedar trunks. In the middle, the visitors sit on the long low wooden platform bench with their backs to us, looking out at the red maples; they turn their heads to chat, one lifts a small teacup, and the tea box on the bench stays beside them. The two people further right on the same bench, one in a dark blue coat, lean toward each other and talk. The old cut stump stays in front of the bench and the round green shrubs sway gently. At the bottom right, the small man in blue whose head and shoulders show above the slope climbs slowly up into view. The purple-leaved maple on the right shakes its branches in the wind.
scenes.11: A few fine snowflakes drift down through the dark grey sky. In the middle, the two people under the black umbrella and the yellow umbrella walk slowly along the snowy causeway toward the small stone arched bridge, leaning into the cold wind and tilting their umbrellas. The bare willow on the left sways, and a little powdery snow slips from its drooping branches. The tall brown standing stone with its small fence, the wooden signpost, the stone embankments and the red-walled hall under its snowy roof in the distance stay where they are. The water under the arched bridge ripples gently and its dark reflection wavers.
scenes.13: Fine snow drifts down through the grey-blue sky. In the foreground the two women walk slowly along the snowy path and talk: the one in the purple coat with the red scarf carries her closed dark umbrella, and the one wearing the purple hood carries her closed yellow umbrella, their sleeves and hems stirring in the cold wind. Behind them on the left, the small figures beside the red box move slowly along the snowy road past the thatched house and its fence. The long wooden bridge curves over the canal on the right, and the dark water beneath it ripples slightly. A little powdery snow slips from the branches of the tree at the top left.
scenes.14: Fine snow falls steadily. Under the great snow-covered stone torii, the woman in the green kimono walks slowly toward us along the snowy approach, holding her open yellow umbrella tilted against the snow, and the small white dog trots beside her feet. The rows of tall stone lanterns capped with snow line both sides and stay in place. A fine powder of snow slips off the heavy dark cedar branches above. Far down the approach, the red shrine gate with the round white lantern stands in the snow, and the tiny figures near it move slowly.
scenes.15: A soft breeze moves through the tall cedars and pines on both sides, and their branches and the long grass on the banks sway gently. On the dirt path at the left, the woman in the grey kimono holding the yellow parasol and the little girl in the red patterned kimono walk slowly side by side, and the parasol tilts as she looks down at the child. Far down the wide road, the small figure near the white gateway and the red-roofed hall walks slowly. The pale sky and the green trees keep their soft, calm colours.
scenes.16: Inside the dark foundry, seen through the two openings between the heavy wooden beams. On the left, white and red flames roar out of the top of the tall clay furnace and sparks shoot up and scatter; at its base the glowing red molten iron flows out and bursts into a shower of sparks. The man at the far left grips his long pole and watches the fire. On the right, the workers bend and move carefully, carrying the glowing iron to the round moulds on the floor and pouring it in, while the men at the back lean over their moulds. The shadows of the figures behind the screen on the left flicker in the firelight. The beams, the stone wall and the long shed stay where they are.
scenes.17: After the rain, the clouds drift slowly and the band of yellow and pink light in the sky shimmers. The ferryboat in the foreground, carrying the rickshaw and its passengers, moves slowly forward on the calm river as the boatman at the stern leans on his long pole; the passengers sway gently and turn to talk. The small white-sailed boat in the distance drifts along the far shore. The bird on top of the tall pole in the water ruffles its wings, and the other bird flies slowly across the sky. The small hall on the green bank at the left and the wooden posts in the water stay in place, and the river ripples, breaking up the reflections of the boat.
scenes.18: Night by the sea. The steam locomotive rolls slowly along the stone embankment pulling its carriages; its wheels and rods turn, red sparks and smoke pour from the tall flared smokestack and stream back over the train, and the red headlamp beam flickers. The driver in the lit cab window leans out a little, and the carriage windows glow. The hazy moon shines through the thin clouds, which drift slowly across the dark sky, and the sky stays dark. The telegraph poles and their wires stay in place, the calm sea glints softly, and the distant ships rest on the horizon.
scenes.19: Calm sea off Shinagawa. The large three-masted ship on the left and the paddle steamer on the right ride at anchor and rock very gently on the swell; the flag on the left mast and the loose sails flutter in the breeze, and a thin trail of smoke rises from the steamer's funnel. The small rowboat between them, with its red-clad crew, rows slowly, its oars dipping. The small dark float in the foreground water bobs up and down. The dark clouds on the right roll slowly across the pale sky, the hill on the left stays in place, and the water ripples, breaking up the reflections of the ships.
scenes.20: A breezy afternoon on the road beside the tall cedars. In the foreground, the woman in the brown coat walks slowly toward us leaning on her stick, and the woman seen from behind with the yellow parasol and the red patterned sash walks slowly away, her parasol tilting in the wind. On the left, the tall figure in the long blue robe with the staff steps slowly forward, and the small figures by the little stand with its white signboard shift and turn. The clouds drift across the blue sky, the cedars on the steep bank sway, and the telegraph wires on the tall poles swing slightly. The stone bridge in the distance and the green bushes on the right stay in place.
scenes.21: Dawn at the river, seen from under the eaves of a dark storehouse. The dark storehouse wall and its tiled eaves fill the left side of the picture close to us and stay exactly where they are. The pale sun stays half hidden behind the yellow-edged clouds, and the dark teal clouds drift slowly across the sky. In the middle of the road, the rickshaw puller, a dark figure against the light, jogs a few more steps, slows down and comes to a stop between the shafts of the hooded rickshaw, its two large spoked wheels rolling to rest on the wet road; then he stands catching his breath, his shoulders moving. At the far left, the small dark figure standing on the bank with a long pole over his shoulder shifts his weight and looks out over the river. The row of wooden stakes along the water's edge and the dark, plain pointed rock in the foreground stay where they are. vivid.base_v1:
Bring this Japanese woodblock print to life as a vivid animated scene. It is a print of Meiji-era Tokyo by Kobayashi Kiyochika (1876-1881), placed on a plain beige background.

CAMERA: The camera stays locked on the print for the whole clip, so the print's outer edges never move. Everything inside the picture is free to move.

ACTION: {SCENE}

LIFE: Motion is clearly visible from the very first second and keeps going for the whole clip. People and animals move with readable, natural actions; clothing, hair, banners, branches, water and weather react to movement and wind. Figures may walk further, turn and interact, and other passers-by may move through the scene.

STYLE: It still looks like a moving woodblock print: flat printed colour, carved outlines, paper texture and Kiyochika's palette. Everything belongs to 1870s-1880s Tokyo: period clothing, vehicles and buildings. No photorealism and no 3D rendering.

The flames in the two tall gas lamps in the foreground and in the small lamps further along the bridge flicker, and the paper lanterns carried by the people swing and glow. The silhouettes on the bridge walk slowly in both directions and turn to one another, keeping their size. Far back in the middle, the tall two-storey horse-drawn omnibus, with passengers seated under the canopy on its roof, stays small and in the same place; its horse only shifts its legs and flicks its tail, and the small rickshaw beside it stays where it is. The dark houses with their lit windows, the bridge railings and the posts stay exactly as printed.
scenes.60: The whole picture keeps its muted colours: the dusty pink and pale blue-green sky, the dark brown banks and the grey river; the people and the piles of goods on the right bank stay flat dark silhouettes with no faces and no colours. The fire keeps the way the print draws it — many thin, broken diagonal strokes of red and pink sweeping up to the right, with ragged dark blotches of smoke among them — and it is alive the whole time: those streaks flicker and shift, new strokes flare and fade, and the dark blotches of smoke tumble slowly along with them. Small sparks rise above the burning roofs on the right. On the right bank, right under the fiercest part of the fire, the silhouetted crowd among the piles of goods stirs and shifts: people haul their bundles toward the water's edge, bending low. Across the river at the bottom left, far from the fire, the dark silhouette of the onlooker stands watching and raises an arm toward the blaze. The red glow on the river flickers, and the reflections under the stone bridge shimmer.
scenes.61: The fire and smoke keep the look of the print, drawn in Kiyochika's broken, streaky strokes, but they are alive the whole time: the flames surge, leap up and fall back and change shape at every moment, the smoke keeps billowing and rolling, and sparks and embers keep swirling. The huge billows of dark smoke and red and orange flame roll across the sky from left to right, the second fire on the far right bank flares, and small red sparks swirl through the pale sky over the river. On the road, the people carrying bundles on their backs hurry along with bent backs and short, quick steps, glancing back over their shoulders at the fire. At the water's edge on the right, the two firemen, further from the blaze, stand watching the far bank: one stretches his hand toward the fire and the other turns his head. The hanging paper lantern and the glass street lamp sway in the hot wind, and the river flickers with the firelight.
scenes.62: A night fire seen from Hisamatsu-chō. The whole picture keeps its dark, muted brown-and-grey night colours: the only bright colours are the tiny orange embers in the smoke and the pale paper lanterns. The fire itself is hidden behind the buildings; what fills the sky is a vast cloud of dark brown smoke, drawn in fine streaky strokes and scattered with tiny orange embers. That smoke is alive the whole time: it keeps rolling and billowing upward and to the left, and the embers in it glow, flicker and drift. Every person in the crowd stays a flat dark-brown silhouette with no faces, no colours and no patterns. The crowd in the foreground, closest to the fire, sways and presses forward: heads turn back toward the smoke, shoulders shift, and the pale paper lanterns and the big round bundle bob and swing. On the roof of the storehouse at the right, the small silhouette of the fireman at the edge raises his arm. The dim firelight flickers on the water under the bridge. The storehouses, the ladder, the bridge, the tall lantern on its post and the scattered goods on the bank stay exactly as printed.
scenes.63: The long dark bands of cloud drift slowly across the grey sky, and the thin column of smoke in the middle rises and wavers. The small pale scraps carried by the wind drift across the burnt ground. The flame in the glass of the tall street lamp flickers. The two charred tree trunks, the burnt brick building, the surviving storehouses and all the people walking through the ruins stay exactly as printed.
scenes.64: The pale clouds drift slowly across the blue sky. The bare twigs of the tall leafless tree on the right tremble in the breeze, and the grass on the banks stirs. The narrow canal under the wooden footbridge ripples, and the reflection of the bridge wavers. On the road at the right, the man in the black hat leans on his cane and takes a few slow steps, and the woman with the small child further along walks slowly. The red-brick building with its small tower, the white house, the wooden footbridge and the stone embankments stay exactly as printed.
scenes.67: A summer night on the street at Asakusa Kuramae. The whole picture keeps its dark night colours: the sky stays a dark blue-green, and every person and rickshaw stays a flat dark silhouette with no faces or colours. The flames in the two gas lamps flicker, and the few small yellow star-shaped lights above the long wall on the right twinkle. The crowd of silhouettes on the wide street strolls slowly in both directions, heads turning; the two people in the foreground, seen from behind, shift and turn their heads toward each other; the rickshaw man on the right lifts his shafts and steps forward a little. The tall fire-lookout ladder, the dark buildings, the big rickshaw on the left and the long wall stay exactly as printed.
scenes.68: A night market at Asakusa. The whole picture keeps its dark night colours: the sky stays a dark blue-grey, the crowd seen from behind stays dark silhouettes, and only the stall-keepers lit by the lamps on the left show their pale faces, as printed. The red and white globe lanterns hung on the branching stand at the right sway and glow, and the small flames of the lamps on the stalls flicker. The leaves of the big tree at the top left stir in the night breeze. The crowd moves slowly among the stalls, heads turning, and the stall-keepers lean forward and gesture to their customers. The red temple gate with its great paper lanterns, the tall pine, the five-storey pagoda and the long stall roof stay exactly as printed.
scenes.69: Snow at Sensōji, seen from the red veranda of the main hall. Fine snow falls steadily across the grey sky and the white roofs. The small bell hanging from the eaves at the top sways a little. The snow-laden bare branches of the trees tremble, and a little powdery snow slips from them. At the red railing, the woman in the pale blue kimono with the white shawl turns her head and points out over the snowy grounds, and the small child beside her looks up and tugs at her sleeve. Far off, the small figure under the umbrella walks slowly through the snow. The hexagonal hall, the five-storey pagoda, the red railing and the eaves stay exactly as printed.
scenes.70: A summer night by the river at Imado. The whole picture keeps its quiet evening colours: the dusky blue-green sky and water outside the window and the soft light inside the room. The full moon stays low above the row of dark trees, and the water below it glints. Inside, the woman in the lilac kimono plays her shamisen: her right hand strikes the strings with the plectrum, her left hand moves along the neck, and she sways gently to the music. The iris in the hanging basket on the pillar stirs, and the light of the lamp at the right flickers. The bonsai on the windowsill, the little red table with its potted plants, the sliding door and the pillar stay exactly as printed.
scenes.71: Fireworks by the pond at Ikenohata. The whole picture keeps its deep night colours: the sky and the pond stay dark green, and every person stays a flat black silhouette with no faces or colours. The falling cascades of the fireworks in the upper right keep streaming down, their red, orange and yellow sparks glittering and trailing as they fall. The red-and-white paper lanterns strung on the rope across the middle sway gently, and the rows of small lights along the far shore and their long reflections on the pond shimmer. The row of silhouetted heads along the bottom turns and tilts up toward the fireworks, and the two boys climbing the crossed poles shift their grip and look up. The crossed poles and the dark far shore stay exactly as printed.
scenes.81: Dusk at Asakusa Bridge. The whole picture keeps its evening colours: the grey-blue sky with dark clouds whose edges glow orange, and the pale light on the water under the arch. The clouds drift slowly. The small dark silhouettes crossing the top of the stone bridge walk slowly in both directions. The moored boats in the foreground rock on the ripples, and their tall masts sway. The water under the arch ripples and its bright reflection wavers, and the lit windows of the houses on both banks glow. The stone arched bridge, the houses and the white storehouse stay exactly as printed.
scenes.82: A night at Shin-Yoshiwara. The whole picture keeps its dark night colours: the dark grey-green sky with long streaks of cloud, and the red glow of the rows of windows and lanterns. Every person stays a flat dark silhouette with no faces, no colours and no patterns, and the number of people never changes. On the left there is exactly one rickshaw with exactly one puller between its shafts, and exactly one man carrying a single red paper lantern: that one lantern-carrier runs a few more steps and slows down, his lantern swinging, and no second lantern or second carrier ever appears. In front of the long building on the right, the same small group of silhouettes keeps its places and turns and walks slowly on the spot. The streaks of cloud drift slowly across the sky. The thin bare branches of the tree in the middle, with their few small pale blossoms, sway a little in the night breeze and keep exactly the blossoms they have. The rows of red windows and the round lanterns along the eaves glow and flicker, and the lamp on the post at the right flickers. The buildings, the tall dark post, the fence around the tree and the lamp post stay exactly as printed.
scenes.83: A bright, breezy day at the Kangyōba bazaar in Kyōbashi. The white clouds drift slowly across the blue sky. The long green fronds of the big willow in front sway in the wind, and the pines on the left stir. The paper lanterns hung at the entrances sway. The crowd in front of the building moves naturally: the woman in the purple kimono with the red sash walks slowly toward the entrance; the man in the bowler hat talks with the woman beside him; the children tug at the adults' sleeves; the man with the white parasol tilts it; the rickshaw man beside the red-seated rickshaw on the left straightens up and looks around; and the men in red caps at the far left turn their heads. The brick building with its sign, the white building on the right, the willow's trunk and the rickshaw stay exactly as printed.
scenes.84: A clear day on the Kinokuni slope at Akasaka. The thin streaks of white cloud drift slowly across the blue sky. The leaves of the trees on the left stir, the plants along the top of the green embankment on the right sway in the breeze, and the telegraph wire swings a little. Everything stays at this same distance from us: the people on the road stay small figures in the wide view and keep their places. The two women side by side on the road take a few slow steps, their sleeves and hems swaying, and turn their heads to talk to each other. Further down the slope, the small figures, the man carrying a pole and the rickshaws move slowly, staying small. The green embankment with its fence, the stone posts along the road, the lamp post and the town below stay exactly as printed.
